summary: Two yoga gurus who abused followers: Pierre Bernard, whose Tantrik Order in New York sparked a 1910 sex-cult scandal, and Bikram Choudhury, whose hot-yoga empire in the US hid decades of sexual assault and abuse.

evidence.note: Bernard born Perry Baker in 1876, meets a wandering yogi in Nebraska at 13
Group moves from San Francisco to Seattle in 1906, then to New York City
Bernard as Dr. Warren seduces a teenage patient at his sanitarium
Police raid on the Tantrik townhouse and Bernard's arrest for abduction
Press frenzy turns into a national panic against yoga and Eastern mysticism
Bikram born in Calcutta around 1944, exact date unknown
Bikram teaches in Japan and invents heated rooms there
Bikram's fabricated championships, Nixon story and other self-mythology
Pattern of rapes and assaults of trainee instructors described from lawsuits
Bikram fled the US to avoid depositions, still teaching in India and Mexico

notes: Two primary subjects: part 1 is Bernard, part 2 is Bikram, linked as a lineage of yoga abusers. Transcript gives Bernard's birth as 1876 (some sources say 1875). Vivekananda and early yoga history are background, not subjects. Bernard's later wealthy compound years get only a brief coda. Mexico (Acapulco camp, current teaching) is brief and left out of setting.
